per_policy_guidance.guidance: Validated 0/12 under the fixed final-state exit rule; no reliable operating region was established, so do not select this policy by default. Its documented intended niche is after observed lid release, when a reachable peg displacement dominates, but that expected benefit is not confirmed by validation. Avoid early lid-held/phase-ambiguous states, large or wall-adjacent displacements, and any miss/drop/blocked-lift recovery. A first-pass event occurred transiently in 11/12 runs but was lost by the final state; all 12 finals had retrieve_peg_from_box=false, 8 retained an open cover and 4 ended closed, and 11/12 had IK-unconverged steps. Recognize failure from a low or stationary peg during lift, lack of stable peg/TCP co-motion, abrupt peg-to-TCP change, wall deflection, or repeated IK residual/limit contacts. Do not hand off on finger closure or a transient threshold crossing alone. Handoff to reorient_and_stage_peg only on closed fingers plus peg clearance and stable two-frame peg/TCP co-motion, with the scored terminal additionally requiring peg center >=0.15 m (or insertion) and cover >0.9 rad; no such final handoff was validated for this policy.

Validated 4/12 (33.3%); treat as a limited fallback rather than the default. Use only in its documented niche: the state remains within a demonstrated retrieve phase, the path is reachable, and a modest local TCP/qpos mismatch is the main issue; re-evaluate after each 8-action execution chunk. Avoid large peg displacement, uncertain lid-versus-peg phase, and miss/drop/regrasp recovery. All 8 failed runs ended with retrieve_peg_from_box=false and negligible reported peg movement (at most 3.22e-6 m); 5 also ended with the cover closed, while 3 retained an open cover but still did not pick up the peg. Thus no peg rise/co-motion is the clearest observed failure, alongside local-target oscillation/drift or repeated IK failure/limit contact. Handoff to reorient_and_stage_peg only when closed fingers, peg height above the wall, and stable causal peg/TCP co-motion agree; for validated skill completion also require peg center >=0.15 m (or insertion) and cover >0.9 rad. Closure alone is not evidence of grasp.

Best-supported policy: validated 8/12 (66.7%), so use as the default among this library for in-distribution entries, especially while the fingers may still be coupled to the lid handle or the release/approach phase is ambiguous and two causal frames are available. Every run ended with retrieve_peg_from_box=true and had zero IK-unconverged steps; the 4 failed finals all had the cover effectively closed, whereas the 8 passes retained cover angles above 0.9 rad. Monitor cover retention explicitly—successful pickup alone is insufficient—and treat cover closure, return toward the lid after release, premature closure, stationary peg during lift, or changing peg/TCP offset as failure. Do not assume reliability for large peg displacement, unusual intermediate states, or perturbed hand configurations: its world-absolute output provides no constructed displacement invariance, and no out-of-distribution validation exists. Handoff to reorient_and_stage_peg during the shared lift only after closed fingers, peg clearance above the wall, and stable two-frame peg/TCP co-motion agree; to claim the validated exit, also verify peg center >=0.15 m (or insertion) and cover >0.9 rad.

Validated 3/12 (25%); no reliable state-conditioned slice was demonstrated, so keep non-default despite its intended object-selective translation prior. Consider it only when the lid-handle-versus-peg reference is unambiguous and the translated path is reachable, with reference geometry checked at each 8-action chunk. Avoid ambiguous/unusual intermediate states, arbitrary peg-rotation changes, and recovery from miss, drop, or cover closure. Of the 9 failures, 5 retained an open cover but had retrieve_peg_from_box=false with only 0-0.0124 m reported peg movement; the other 4 ended with the cover effectively closed after 0.730-0.773 m reported peg movement. IK-unconverged steps occurred in 6/12 runs, including all four of those cover-closed/high-movement failures. Recognize failure from a reference-induced target jump, continued lid attachment, offset descent, peg staying low or separating from the TCP, cover angle <=0.9 rad, or persistent IK/limit issues. Handoff to reorient_and_stage_peg only on closed fingers, peg above the wall with margin, and stable two-frame co-motion; validated completion additionally requires peg center >=0.15 m (or insertion) and cover >0.9 rad.

summary:
Validation is strictly in distribution: each policy ran from the entry state of its own 530-step training segment in all 12 demonstrations, with a 795-step budget and its training-time arguments. No out-of-distribution or recovery result exists. Final success rates were h03 8/12, h02 4/12, h04 3/12, and h01 0/12. Therefore use h03 as the best-supported default, reserve h02 for a clearly modest local hand/configuration mismatch, and keep h04 and especially h01 non-default unless an external reason justifies an unvalidated specialization. All policies take `{}` call arguments.

Use the fixed terminal check consistently: peg center at least 0.15 m high (or inserted) and cover angle >0.9 rad at the final state. For handoff to reorient_and_stage_peg, also require the shared carrying evidence in the documents: closed fingers, peg above the box wall, and stable peg-to-TCP relation while both move across two causal frames. Finger closure alone is never contact truth. If the peg stays low, fails to co-move, is missed/dropped, IK repeatedly fails, or the cover closes, do not claim success or assume recovery; stop or invoke a separately validated skill. In particular, h03’s only observed final failure pattern was cover closure despite recorded retrieval, making cover monitoring the main library-level safeguard.
